newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Caltex sees Philippine petroleum usage up 8-9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Caltex sees Philippine petroleum usage up 8-9 pct.

text.p: Petroleum consumption in the Philippines will rise eight to nine percent this year compared to 1995 levels, Caltex Philippines president William Tiffany said on Thursday.
Existing consumption levels were at 350,000 barrels per day, Tiffany told a news conference.
Caltex Philippines is a unit of Caltex Petroleum Corp, a joint venture of U.S. oil majors Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
"There's a lot of pent up demand with people committing to invest in the country, especially in the transport sector," Tiffany said.
Caltex Petroleum Corp Chairman David Law-Smith, visiting the Philippines, said the oil industry had under estimated growth in Asia.
"Asia is short (of petroleum products) but the rest of the world is in surplus. This we believe will balance out," he said.
On Monday Law-Smith told Reuters in Singapore that Caltex was planning to invest $5.0 billion in Asia by 2000.
Last month, Tiffany had announced that Caltex would spend $500 million over the next five years to enhance its marketing and refinery facilities in the Philippines.
